betterquesting:10.desc:8:
When crops breed, the resulting stats are the rounded-down average of the parents' stats plus a a random value.

The range of random values you get depends on 2 factors: the number of parents and the amount of fertilizer stored within them.

Spreading from a single parent rarely produces much in terms of changes, but breeding using 2 or more parents can net you a lot of progress.

Similarly applying fertilizer increases the amount amount of stat variation you can get from breeding and can even prevent stat loss when applied by a Crop Manager.

Multiple parent:
- 0 to 49 fertilizer: -1 -> +1 (higher chance for -1 and 1)
- 50-100 fertilizer: -2 -> +2
- 101+ fertilizer: 0 -> +4 (40% chance for 0)

Single parent:
- 0-49 fertilizer: -1 -> 0 (higher chance for 0)
- 50-100 fertilizer: no variation
- 100+ fertilizer: 0 -> 1 (higher chance for 0)

Deterministic breeding is similar to how bees work, where you must bring the right species together. Some situations require more than two parents, though at the early stages of crops, controlled random mutations will often be more practical.

[note]Advanced crops (§5MV§r and above materials) will require the breeding machine.[/note]

Most crops will also have access to breeding pools. Breeding pools are like a set of tags associated with each crop. When breeding, if none of the parents produce a deterministic mutation, but some share one or more breeding pools, a random mutation may occur. The resulting offspring will always be a species tagged with one of the shared pools.

[note]Once you've obtained your first 31/31/31 seed, it can be helpful to use these random pool mutations to collect many different types of crops.[/note]
